messages.body_plain:
At least some of the binaries are now up, including r-release ones for Mac and Windows:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rexpokit/index.html

Cheers,
Nick

>
> "‘rexpokit’ was installed before R 4.0.0: please re-install it".
>

messages.subject: num_cores_to_use ignored
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

When running BioBeoBEARS analyses on our server, the actual input for the num_cores_to_use setting is ignored and the process instead uses all available cores.
When I set BioGeoBEARS_run_object$num_cores_to_use = 12 (or any other number), the analysis will use the total amount of 64 cores.
This server is shared between users and this would limit other users when this analysis takes up all the cores.

Kind regards,
Sander

The more common issue is e.g. R.app will only do 1 core no matter what the setting is. If you want you can search the code files on num_cores_to_use and find the exact line that opens the processors, and try playing with that command on the server to see if it is malfunctioning.  It is part of R's snow package I think.

Nick

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Transtitions
messages.body_plain:
Hi Natalia,

In order to make this kind of inference, first you need to perform biogeographic stochastic mapping. Without that, the estimates are probabilities (node 1 may have a 60% probability of having area A, and a 40% probability of being in area B -- thus you do not really know in which area it was). Stochastic mapping forcibly resolves the ancestral states in accordance with the original probabilities, and then you can count the number of transitions. Because it is stochastic, you have to run a large number of replicates for each estimate (e.g. 100), and summarize across the results.

Please check this wiki with the example script by Nick:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeographical-stochastic-mapping-example-script

The original paper describing biogeographic stochastic mapping:
https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/jbi.12898

You might also want to check this paper where we provide a script to perform stochastic mapping over a sample of trees, so that both biogeographic and phylogenetic uncertainties are taken into account:
https://www.mdpi.com/1424-2818/13/9/418

Best,
Ivan
